stem:
Hydroxyethanal, $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CHO}$, has been observed in dust clouds near the centre of our galaxy.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Predict the bond angles labelled $x$ and $y$ in the diagram of hydroxyethanal.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Hydroxyethanal reacts separately with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH) and with Tollens' reagent.

State what you would observe in each reaction.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Hydroxyethanal is converted to ethanedioic acid, $(\text{CO}_2\text{H})_2$, when it reacts with excess acidified dichromate(VI) ions, $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$.
parts.text: State the role of acidified $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ in this reaction.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain any other necessary conditions for this reaction to be successful.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
Hydroxyethanal can be reduced to ethane-1,2-diol, $(\text{CH}_2\text{OH})_2$, as shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}
parts.text:
Write an equation for the reduction of hydroxyethanal to $(\text{CH}_2\text{OH})_2$.

Use $[\text{H}]$ to represent an atom of hydrogen from the reducing agent.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Identify a reagent for this reduction reaction.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
$(\text{CH}_2\text{OH})_2$ also forms when an alkene $\mathbf{A}$ reacts with cold, dilute, acidified manganate(VII) ions.

Name $\mathbf{A}$.
